title: Post-install assertions
description: What must be true of the running instance for it to match the plan that produced it. Apply promises something; these are what proves it. This is the least settled of the seven files: its consumer is the verify step, which is built in Phase A, and the schema is expected to gain detail there.

id.description: A namespaced identifier, unique across the profile.

kind.description: What the check reads back. The kinds are properties of a running database service in general, which is why the core can carry them without knowing which engine is running.

expr.description: An expression over what was read back and what the plan promised. Absent means the kind is assertion enough on its own.

remediation.description: What to do when the instance does not match its plan. A verify failure is loud, because it means the instance is no longer what the documentation claims.
